commitResults.messageBody:
The index page was for AB3.

Let's:
* Swap out the CI status and CodeCov badges for Sieve's one
* Change the product description to suit Sieve
* Add in an acknowledgement for the source code
Update DG product scope and acknowledgements

Sieve's target users are tutors teaching local Singapore students,
whose phone numbers are 8 digits. AB3 accepted any run of 3 or more
digits.

Let's strip all non-digit characters before validating, so formatted input
such as "9123 4567" or "(9123)-4567" is accepted and stored as
"91234567".

Storing only digits lets duplicate detection compare phones reliably.

Strip in both ParserUtil and JsonAdaptedPerson, so a data file with a
hand-edited, formatted phone still loads instead of being discarded.
The Phone constructor stays strict and accepts only 8 digits.

Require 8-digit phone numbers

Sieve's target users are tutors teaching local Singapore students,
whose phone numbers are 8 digits. AB3 accepts any run of 3 or more
digits.

Require exactly 8 digits after removing whitespace, hyphens and
parentheses, so commonly formatted input such as "9123 4567" or
"(9123)-4567" is accepted and stored as "91234567". Keep all other
characters, including '+', so that a number with a country code such
as "+65 811878" is rejected instead of shrinking into a valid-looking
8-digit number.

Strip in both ParserUtil and JsonAdaptedPerson, so a data file with a
hand-edited, formatted phone still loads instead of being discarded.
The Phone constructor stays strict and accepts only 8 digits.

Update test fixtures to use 8-digit phones, and add tests for
stripping, rejected input and loading formatted phones from JSON.

Addresses accept any length, so a very long address stretches the
client card in the UI. Repeated whitespace typed or pasted into an
address is also stored as is.

Trim the ends and collapse consecutive whitespace into a single space,
then reject addresses longer than 150 characters. Check the length
after collapsing, so stray spaces do not count against the limit.

Normalize in both ParserUtil and JsonAdaptedPerson, so a hand-edited
address with extra whitespace or a line break in the data file still
loads.

Names accept only alphanumeric characters and spaces, so real names
such as "O'Brien", "Nur-Aisyah" or "David Ray Jr." are rejected,
while input starting with a digit or symbol is accepted.

Require names to start with a letter, followed by letters, digits,
spaces, hyphens, apostrophes and full stops, up to 50 characters.
Keep '/' disallowed, as it is the prefix delimiter, so a name such
as "a/l" cannot be misread as an address.

Trim the ends and collapse consecutive whitespace before validating,
in both ParserUtil and JsonAdaptedPerson, so a hand-edited name with
extra spaces in the data file still loads.

The invalid email message lists every local-part and domain rule over
11 lines, which is hard to read in the result display and does not
show what a valid email looks like.

Replace it with a one-line message and an example address. The
validation rules themselves are unchanged.
Update the help text to list all commands and resolved the issue where when the help window is minimised, entering the help command will not reopen the help window, instead it remains minimised.
